facts.text: The repository contains example reinforcement-learning environments for the NVIDIA Isaac Gym
Isaac Gym itself is a separate Preview 4 download installed before this repository, so the simulator is external to the clone
The public factory is isaacgymenvs.make(seed, task, num_envs, sim_device, ...)
The documented Ant example calls isaacgymenvs.make(seed=0, task="Ant", num_envs=..., sim_device="cuda:0", rl_device="cuda:0")
Ant is the task class behind task="Ant": class Ant(VecTask)
Ant sets numObservations to 60 and numActions to 8

The observation concatenates 1 torso height, 3 local velocities, 3 local angular velocities, yaw, roll, target angle, up projection, heading projection, 8 scaled joint positions, 8 scaled joint velocities, 24 contact-force values and 8 actions (60 values)
The observation space is a Box from -inf to +inf over num_observations values
The action space is a Box from -1 to 1 over num_actions values
The Ant configuration sets clipActions to 1.0
VecTask.step clamps every action to -clip_actions .. clip_actions before applying it
The Ant episode length is 1000 control steps
An agent is reset when its progress reaches max_episode_length - 1, or when its torso height falls below termination_height
The Ant termination height is 0.31 and a fallen agent receives the death cost
A fallen agent (torso height below termination_height) is reset
The Ant timestep is dt=0.0166 s (1/60 s)
Ant takes its dt from the simulation configuration
A reset draws joint positions uniformly from -0.2 to 0.2 and joint velocities uniformly from -0.1 to 0.1
The install requires gym==0.23.1, the legacy Gym API

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the test data of the fake; its kinematic transitions are deterministic, so one seed repeats a trajectory.  The upstream Ant reset uses torch's random generator and the Isaac Gym physics engine, so this fake does not reproduce upstream trajectories.

fidelity.engine: isaacgymenvs:Ant (kinematic stand-in for the Isaac Gym Ant task)
gaps: the fake has no rigid-body dynamics, no contacts, no actuators and no Isaac Gym physics: joint positions and the torso height follow a simple kinematic rule, so forces and contact behaviour are not modelled
the fake returns a 60-element observation in the upstream layout but fills the contact-force block with zeros and derives the root and joint values from test data, not from simulation

the upstream VecTask.step returns (obs_dict, reward, reset, info) from the legacy Gym API while the fake returns the Gymnasium five-tuple; the bridge accepts both, and the real isaacgymenvs.make path was never run because Isaac Gym Preview 4 is external and needs a CUDA device
the fake models one environment, while isaacgymenvs.make returns a vectorised environment of num_envs copies (4096 by default in the Ant configuration)
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop the runtime refuses step and reset until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, while the last observation stays readable; there is no actuator to stop
